<explanation>
The first heading establishes food-seasoning purpose. The ingredients heading makes the counted tissue and scraps food ingredients for the dog; "it" and "them" resolve to that piece and those two scraps. Cutting applies to each part and to both together: keep each partial cutting subject and the complete shared action. The partial actions do not replace their expressed combination. The complete cutting subject belongs below each partial action and below the complete ingredient group; the reverse directions lose a material or action restriction. Each complete source subject appears beneath every compatible parent copy, including both Dog food branches. An entry already represents a source subject with the same meaning; the complete shared cutting action has no identical descendant, but still appears beneath every compatible group and partial-action occurrence. Salt and connective tissue can have nonfood uses. Tissue "for the dog" specifies a recipient, not a food role; it could be for a training scent. Those unrestricted headings stay outside Food and Dog food. Separate Salt, Connective tissue, Meat scraps and Dogs subjects remain alongside the actions. The separate recipient clause adds no ingredient relationship.
</explanation>
